items.title: 68239_Ram Ramirez oral history interview
items.q: Teddy Hill had this beautiful book that they were playing, you know. Teddy had a really gorgeous book, with Roy Eldridge, you know, and Chu Berry... He had a nice little band, you know, and he had beautiful arrangements!

ctx.x: Yeah. And we also are speaking about bands that, when they came to New York, their music changed, and they had to get arrangements with much more variations than the Blues, you know -- more kind of things. Here you had bands like Don Redman, Benny Carter, Teddy Hill, Fletcher Henderson, and these bands had arrangements of all types. Because I mean, for you to be playing the Blues all night, it wasn't really compatible with the Eastern...with Harlemites, I would say. They wanted to hear other things, too, you…
